newsitem.title: SPAIN: Size of Endesa sale undecided - govt source.
newsitem.headline: Size of Endesa sale undecided - govt source.

text.p: Spain may well decide to sell more than 25 percent of Empresa Nacional de Electricidad (Endesa) on the stock market this autumn, but the size of the offer has not been decided, an official source said on Tuesday.

State holding company SEPI has a 67 percent stake in Endesa, valued at roughly one and a half trillion pesetas. Initially the government said it would fully privatise the company in three stages, starting this year.

"Everything depends on the capacity of the market to absorb the offer. Originally the government had set a limit of 25 percent for this year's placement, but seeing how well the Telefonica and Repsol offers were received, it became clear that there is tremendous demand out there, and there's room for a bigger stake," the source told Reuters.

The February sale of a remaining 20.9 percent stake in Telefonica was nine time oversubscribed on the retail tranche, while press reports say Repsol's current retail share offer was oversubscribed up to 17 times as of last Friday.
"The market has a tremendous capacity to absorb this kind of an offer, and there's obviously not going to be a problem to sell a bigger stake. Endesa is a very solid company," he said.
Details of the offer are not likely to be made public before September, although the organisation of the sale is already underway, he added.
SEPI chairman Pedro Ferreras said last week that the government may privatise up to 40 percent of the electricity giant this year.
